newsitem.title: CHINA: Survey says fake goods "everywhere" in China.
newsitem.headline: Survey says fake goods "everywhere" in China.

text.p: Fakes may be faulty but they are fashionable and favoured in China.
A survey showed that 68 percent of residents of the boomtowns of Shanghai and Guangzhou said fake goods were "everywhere", the official Xinhua news agency said late on Thursday.
Eighty percent said they had bought fake goods, it said. The most frequently seen counterfeit goods were brand-name clothing, foods and drink, medicine and audio-visual products.
China has come under fire from foreign governments and companies accusing Beijing of not doing enough to combat the counterfeiting of brand-name goods.
In June, China and the United States narrowly averted a multi-billion dollar trade war over U.S. accusations of rampant Chinese piracy of software, music and videos.

The survey showed that 29.3 percent of respondents thought much-publicised government crackdowns on the sale of fake or shoddy goods was "fruitless", Xinhua said. Nearly 62 percent thought such sweeps were "only partially effective".
More than 71 percent of those surveyed said new laws should be adopted to try to curb sales of fake goods and 55 percent said more consumer awareness was needed, it said.
